minutes.headline: Select Board appoints a housing authority tenant member and directs town counsel to seek an injunction over boulders.
minutes.summary: The board held a joint interview and vote with the housing authority, approved a liquor license officer change, ratified two hires, and debated how to remove boulders from a town right-of-way. It also ranked FY2023 legislative priorities, opened the town meeting warrant, adopted a revised charge for the municipal building design committee, and updated a COVID sick leave policy.

public_comment.topic: A parks commission member reminded everyone of Thursday's Marshall Park meeting with architects and engineers.
Chair asked for public comment at start; none given.

votes.motion: Appoint Wayne Caron to the Lunenburg Housing Authority tenant seat, term expiring 2023 (joint vote).
Approve change of officers for Global Montello Group Corp. (Honey Farms) license.
Ratify appointment of Joel Ortega as full-time officer effective July 25, 2022.
Ratify appointment of Benjamin McGinnis as van driver.
Follow town counsel's recommendation to seek a superior court injunction to remove the boulders at 993 Massachusetts Avenue.
Open the annual town meeting warrant January 12, 2022 and close it March 21, 2022 at 4 p.m.
Approve changes to the emergency paid sick leave policy.
Adopt revised charge for the Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee with two wording changes.

what_happened.line: The board voted to follow town counsel's recommendation to seek a superior court injunction to remove boulders from a town right-of-way at 993 Massachusetts Avenue.
In a joint vote with the housing authority, the board unanimously appointed Wayne Caron to the tenant seat on the Lunenburg Housing Authority.
The board agreed on an order of FY2023 priorities to put to legislators, led by the Flat Hill Road culvert and old primary school abatement, and dropped two candidates.
The board opened the annual town meeting warrant for January 12, 2022 and set it to close March 21, 2022 at 4 p.m.
The board approved changes to the emergency paid sick leave policy and adopted a revised charge for the Municipal Building Design Committee.

why_it_matters: The boulder dispute may lead to a court case, and the minutes leave the cost of filing and any court costs unclear, so it could draw on town funds.

The priority list sets which capital projects, such as the culvert and the old primary school abatement, the town asks state legislators to fund, and that affects what residents may later be asked to pay for locally.
The open warrant is how articles reach the March town meeting, where residents vote on spending.
watch_next: The town meeting warrant opens January 12, 2022 and closes March 21, 2022 at 4 p.m.
Policy meetings on liquor regulations, boot drives and a commemorative policy are to be scheduled.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all eight non-procedural votes and on most figures and decisions. The main differences are that our minutes call the Joel Ortega vote a ratification where the official minutes call it a revote, and that several figures and decisions appear in only one record.
